[background] Lithium-ion diffusivity of different coating materials at 300K.
- [background] The term “am ”means amorphous while “cry ”means crystalline.
- [background] compares the functionality and the role of coatings in conventional and solid-state batteries (SSB).
- [background, negated] As previously mentioned, it was earlier speculated that the interface between cathode and SE in an SSB might be very stable, which how-ever was later proved incorrect.
- [background] Some experts have even pointed out that the interfaces in SSBs are more complex in contrast to the conven-tional lithium-ion batteries as illustrated in Fig. 11 [199] .
- [interpretation] Additionally, the coating layer would also replace the original cathode/SE interface while generating two new interfaces know as cathode/coating and coat-ing/SE interface.
- [background] Since the exact nature of these interfaces is not well understood, in addition to there being very limited data; systematic re-search efforts would be required to understand their role in SSB battery operations.
- [background] Inorganic SEs can be divided into three main categories, (1) ox-ides, (2) sulfides and (3) argyrodites.

- [background] Sulfide based SEs are of immense significance due to their exceptionally high ionic conductivities when compared to oxide-based SEs.
- [background] Unlike oxides, sulfide-based SE have low chemical stability and are only stable in a narrow voltage window [196] .
- [interpretation] This make it difficult for sulfide SEs to be employed in practical SSB due to the limited amount of energy density delivered in the limited oper-ational voltage window.
- [background] Additionally, the sulfide-based SEs form resis-tive interfaces when in direct contact with the cathode material and thus an increase in interfacial resistance is generally observed.
- [background] However, to successfully employ them in SSBs, applying surface coatings on cath-ode materials are considered a promising alternative to overcome their intrinsic electrochemical stability issues.
- [background] Thus, the proper selection of coating materials and interface design are challenging tasks in SSB re-search.
- [background] Some of the many different coatings that have been applied to cathodes in SSBs include LiNbO3, LiTaO3, LiBO2, Li4Ti5O12 , Li2O-TiO2, ZrO2 , SiO2, Li2SiO3, Li4GeO4 , Li3PO4 , Al2O3 etc. and have resulted in considerable performance enhancements in all SSB cells [ 144 , 200–207 ].
